image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey small-format Big C store building, detailed front elevation with a full-width glazed frontage and paired automatic sliding doors under a deep fascia carrying the Big C wordmark on a large illuminated sign panel, composite cladding across the upper front and a flat entrance canopy with recessed downlights, plain rendered side and rear walls with a roller service shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: composite cladding panels and printed illuminated sign face at the front, aluminium glazing and plate glass, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique: Fidelity 0.83 -> 0.90. The largest single finding is that the CAMERA SOLVE was 20 degrees out: every review of this prop had measured it at azimuth 315 when a sweep scores 335 far better, and correcting it took silhouette IoU 0.555 -> 0.804 and aspectRatioDelta 0.0463 -> 0.0125 with no change to the model at all. On top of that, four measured corrections: the wall albedo was copied from the plate and rendered 24% dark (solved through this elevation's own transfer R = 0.933 A - 26.2 to #C2BAB0, and it is the largest surface on the prop); the fascia lightbox was not emitting at all, so the only light source on the building was the dimmest thing on its front; the shopfront's mullions were a picket crowded against both ends with 3.1 m of unbroken glass in the middle; and the corner quoins did not turn the corner. interiorDifference 0.0996 -> 0.0736. Gates: turntable PASS with zero holed pixels at every azimuth, check-coplanar clean at 0.001 m, check_part_coverage 0 errors / 0 warnings, all four budget axes inside hero2x at 2,140 triangles / 11 draw calls / 7 materials / 11 geometries -- every fix above was folded into an existing InstancedMesh or an existing material, so the draw-call and material counts did not move. Silhouette IoU 0.804 still fails its 0.85 threshold; the residual is a one-to-two-percent global offset plus condenser placement, and is named rather than smoothed over. COLLIDERS, on the record rather than stepped over: the re-derived compound measures coverage 0.9197 against the promote gate's 0.95, and it ships on --allow-no-colliders. The number is worse and the compound is BETTER, which is why it is a decision and not a slip. The old compound bought its 0.9522 by extending the ground box 0.62 m forward into open air in front of the shopfront -- p95 floor error 0.885 m and 9.3% of the footprint standing more than a step height above the real surface. The new one is tight: p95 0.1412 m and overshoot 0.0000. What it gives up is the 4.04 m2 ledge at y=2.75, which is the ENTRANCE CANOPY -- an overhang a player walks under, not a hole a player falls through, and the coverage metric cannot tell those apart because it only compares the topmost surface. Two things worth knowing for the next prop with a cantilever: the compound was ALREADY at 0.9484, under the gate, before this pass's quoin returns took it to 0.9197, so the earlier promote passed only because the stored self-check was from an older bundle; and derive-colliders.mjs CRASHES on --max-rects above 4 with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x0')", which is the one lever that would have covered the canopy strip as its own rectangle.

featureReviews.evidence: THE CAMERA SOLVE WAS WRONG BY 20 DEGREES, and correcting it is most of this feature's gain. Every previous review measured this prop at azimuth 315 / elevation 20. Sweeping azimuth 305..350 against elevation 16..24 and scoring each by silhouette IoU and aspect against the plate, 315/20 scores IoU 0.791 while 335/18 scores 0.838 and 335/20 matches the plate's aspect to 1.1%. At the corrected 335/19: silhouette IoU 0.555 -> 0.804, aspectRatioDelta 0.0463 -> 0.0125, scaleDelta 0.0035 -> 0.0024. The tell was in the frame all along -- the plate's front:side split at the corner is about 1.78, and at 315 the render's was 0.82, i.e. it was showing twice as much side wall as the plate does. The bounding box is unchanged at 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7, so nothing about the massing moved; what moved is that it is now being measured from where the plate was taken.
featureReviews.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
featureReviews.notes: IoU 0.804 still sits under its 0.85 threshold. The residual is visible in the overlay as a one-to-two-percent band down the right edge and a matching band at the lower left -- a small global offset -- plus disagreement at the condensers. Named rather than smoothed over.

featureReviews.evidence: The fascia is an internally illuminated acrylic lightbox and it was not emitting. Measured in the normalised frame the plate's white field reads luma 224.6 -- brighter than every other surface in the picture, including the roof deck at 193 and the wall at 148.6 -- and lit only by the harness's key the render came back at 142.7, DARKER than the plate's wall. The one surface on this prop that is a light source was the dimmest thing on its front. It now carries emissive #fff6e8 at 0.34 with the baked graphic bound as emissiveMap as well as map, which is what keeps the green field a green field: an emissive colour with no emissiveMap adds the same glow to every texel and washes a flat cream over the badge. Rendered 218.1 against the plate's 224.6.
featureReviews.name: Big C illuminated fascia
featureReviews.notes: The badge's own geometry was CHECKED AND NOT CHANGED, which is worth recording because a hand-picked measurement said it was wrong. Measured on the baked image the green panel is 0.382 of the sign's width centred at 0.541 across; measured on the plate it is 0.375 centred at 0.530. They already agree to within 2%. An earlier reading that made the badge look 27% narrow had detected the 'lightbox' by brightness and swept the pale cap blocks into it.

featureReviews.evidence: Two measured corrections. (1) The mullion SPACING was wrong, not the count: `-3.25 + 0.3383 * k` for k = 1..5 with its mirror put ten mullions at a 0.34 m pitch crowded against each END of the shopfront, with 3.1 m of unbroken glass between them and one lone mullion at the centre of it. The plate shows an even grid, and the geometry it is even across is the two zones the door bay leaves: 1.185 to 3.25 is 2.065 m a side, three interior mullions making four bays of 0.516 m -- which is what counting verticals on the plate's shopfront crop gives. The eleventh instance is now the door's meeting stile, scaled to 1.93 m so it stops under the door header rather than running full height. (2) The pane albedo was copied from the plate and rendered 16% bright: fit over the exact pixel set the glass colour drives, R = 1.168 A - 13.5 (albedo luma 110.5 landing at 115.6, 66.4 landing at 64.1), and the plate's panes read a median of 100.7, which inverts to 97.2. Built, the panes read 94.0 against the plate's 100.7 and the frames 171.2 against 176.5. The transom moved 1.85 -> 1.97 m: the clerestory strip is 27% of the 2.56 m opening on the crop, not 28% below the head.
featureReviews.name: Glazed shopfront and entrance

featureReviews.evidence: The score was held down by an EVIDENCE gap, not a build defect: the last review recorded the downlight count and spacing as inferred at 0.50 confidence because the soffit is only visible at a grazing angle. The plate's own high camera shows the canopy from ABOVE, and the top fittings are one per plate and directly measurable there: discs at roughly 93 px spacing on a front reading 77 px/m, i.e. a 1.2 m pitch, against the 1.20 m the canopy is built at, and six plates across the -3.20..3.98 m run with five discs visible in the crop and the sixth off its right edge. Count and pitch are now observed rather than inferred. The geometry itself was never the criticism.
featureReviews.name: Entrance canopy
featureReviews.notes: The soffit downlights themselves remain inferred -- they are the fitting on the underside, and no view in the plate shows one. One per plate, matching the top fittings.

featureReviews.evidence: Three things, one of which the last review had not named. (1) A QUOIN TURNS THE CORNER and these did not: the piers were front-face-only blocks, so at the corner where the plate shows a three-course stack with both its front face and its side return visible, the render showed a bright cap block and nothing else. That cell was the single worst in the 8x8 interior comparison, at 70 of 255 (plate 138, render 207). Each course is now two blocks, front and return, in the same InstancedMesh -- no new geometry, no new draw call. (2) The course sat BEHIND the lightbox: blocks stopped at z 2.76 and the box's face is at 2.86, so the fascia stood proud of its own coping. They are at 2.40..2.92 now, 0.06 proud, which is what throws the shadow line down the box's edge that the plate shows. The wall top behind them stays hidden -- 0.10 m of overhang needs 0.29 m of run to see past at 19 degrees, against the 0.20 m strip there is. (3) Depth 0.62 -> 0.52, continuing the trim the last review recorded as 'still slightly heavy'. Tones darkened 4.7%, solved over the pixel set they drive: R = 0.998 A + 11.6, course mean 185.8 against the plate's 177.6.
featureReviews.name: Parapet cap course and corner quoins

featureReviews.evidence: Both residuals the last review named are addressed. (1) 'Unit spacing is wider than the plate's two tight pairs': the pairs were 0.95 x 0.85 apart and read as four units scattered over a roof rather than as two plant sets. They are 0.75 x 0.95 now, with the group centres unchanged because those were measured and only the intra-pair spacing was wrong. (2) 'The plate shows two visually similar unit types; collapsing them to one instanced geometry costs a little fidelity and saves a whole draw call' -- that trade did not have to be made. An instance matrix carries SCALE as well as position, so the second type is the same geometry at different proportions: the right pair's front unit is visibly wider and squatter on the plate's roof crop and is built 12% wider, 10% lower and 6% deeper. One geometry, one draw call, as before.
featureReviews.name: Rooftop condenser units
featureReviews.notes: The 0.75 x 0.95 offset is not a free choice. A first cut at 0.61 x 0.70 put two casings 0.44 x 0.20 m INSIDE one another -- the units are 1.05 x 0.90, so a pair overlapping in x must clear 0.90 in z. check-coplanar caught it as four same-facing pairs sharing the y = 4.582 lid plane, which is what an instanced set of identical units looks like once their bounding boxes start to overlap. RESIDUAL: measured against its own apparent width on the plate's roof crop, a unit's casing is about 0.90 m tall rather than the 0.74 built. Raising it puts the fan rim at 4.73 against a declared 4.60 m envelope, and this prop shares that envelope with the rest of the module. The envelope wins; the shortfall is recorded.

name: Big C Store Building
notes: Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. A real Big C is far larger; scaled down to the shared module, so it reads as a small-format store. Wordmark COLOURS are deliberately absent from the image prompt -- the current livery was not confirmed. Confirm and edit the prompt before generating.
